subject: Instrumenting Redwood inference runtime for partner observability — scope, SOW and handoff
messages:
From: Pete Lang <pete@observaconsult.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, KarThik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observa proposed scope for instrumentation & partner handoff

Hi Neha / KarThik —

Thanks for the time yesterday. Per our call, I attached a first-draft scope that covers:
- runtime metrics (latency, p99/p95 by model & route)
- KV/cache hit ratios and prefix cache telemetry
- device-level GPU metrics and token-level attribution
- OTLP export shape for Grafana and Datadog sinks

Two quick asks before we finalize the SOW:
1) Confirm the list of in-scope endpoints and model variants you want Observa to instrument in the pilot (we included the hosted API + Dedicated GPU pool).
2) Point me at the relevant runbooks or owners for alert thresholds (we used your default latency SLOs in the draft).

Attaching: instrumentation-scope.pdf (draft) and a short SOW template. Happy to take comments inline.

Best,
Pete
Principal Engineer, Observa Consulting

Attachments: instrumentation-scope.pdf (PDF, 154KB), SOW-Observa-Redwood-v1.docx (DOCX, 72KB)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Pete Lang <pete@observaconsult.com>
Cc: KarThik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observa proposed scope for instrumentation & partner handoff

Pete — thanks for the draft. Quick responses inline:

- Pilot targets: hosted API (text-gen, chat) and one Dedicated pool (p3-8x large) across us-west-2.
- Owners: KarThik will own the runtime hooks; Vanessa will own dashboarding/consumer UX for the partner-facing dashboards.
- Alert thresholds: we use p99 < 250ms for short sequences, p99 < 750ms for long sequences — see baseline in our SLO doc.

Can you update the SOW to call out:
- explicit OTLP fields we need for token attribution (field names in the draft)
- a 2-week knowledge transfer window and a one-month support warranty after handoff

Looping KarThik and Vanessa to add technical detail. Also cc'ing Alex Turner from Grafana so they can confirm the OTLP shape.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

---
Neha's signature
Redwood Inference

From: KarThik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Pete Lang <pete@observaconsult.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@grafana.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 10:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observa proposed scope for instrumentation & partner handoff

Pete / team — added a few technical notes after walking the runtime:

- We can emit token attribution via an additional OTLP span attribute called "redwood.token.index" and a metric label "route_id". That covers cost-by-route and per-token latency.
- For GPU telemetry we prefer per-device exporter (NVIDIA DCGM) + a lightweight exporter that correlates with request IDs.
- For prefix/KV cache hits: we'll emit metrics at the cache layer with a 1s scrape window — this is important to avoid overcounting.

I've dropped short comments into the Drive scope doc: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aB2cD_instrumentation_scope

Two items for your SOW update:
1) Add Grafana dashboard templates (we'll want a sample Grafana .json and a Datadog notebook).
2) Call out a rollback/fallback plan if instrumentation causes <5% p50 inflation during the pilot.

Happy to sync 30 min if you want to walk the runtime hooks.

-Karthik
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@grafana.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, KarThik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Pete Lang <pete@observaconsult.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observa proposed scope for instrumentation & partner handoff

Thanks for the heads up — Grafana team here: the OTLP shape you suggested looks good. A few notes from Grafana side: 

- We can consume the token attribution attribute; we'll provide a sample dashboard JSON and a Loki log label mapping.
- For hosted customers we recommend a rate-limited OTLP ingest to avoid burst charges — we'll include a recommended batching/ingest config in our example.
- We can also provide a managed dashboard backfill script to map historical metrics to the new schema if you want historical baselines.

I'll attach the Grafana sample dashboard and a short ingest config snippet. Happy to join the KT session once dates are set.

Best,
Alex Turner
Partner Solutions, Grafana Labs

Attachments: grafana-dashboard-sample.json (JSON, 9KB)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Pete Lang <pete@observaconsult.com>, KarThik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@grafana.com>, Integrations Team <integrations@datadog.com>

Subject: Re: Observa proposed scope for instrumentation & partner handoff

Thanks everyone — this is excellent progress. Next steps and owners: 

- Pete: please update the SOW to reflect Karthik's OTLP attributes, the 2-week KT window, Grafana sample dashboards, and rollback clause. Target revised SOW by EOD Thu 16 Apr. (owner: Pete)
- KarThik: prepare a 30-min KT demo (runtime hooks + local emitter) for Tue 21 Apr. (owner: KarThik)
- Vanessa: draft the partner dashboard UX acceptance criteria and a short consumer-facing README for customers. Due Mon 20 Apr. (owner: Vanessa)
- Alex / Datadog: share any ingest-rate best practices or example config snippets to avoid unexpected charges.

I'll review the revised SOW and route to Contracts (cc: legal once we have the final doc). HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/8271 — tagging this as partner integration.

Thanks — see attachments for the current draft scope.

Neha
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
